pois.name: Glasgow Botanic Gardens
pois.intro: Glasgow Botanic Gardens is a botanical garden located in the West End of Glasgow, Scotland. It features several glasshouses, the most notable of which is the Kibble Palace.

pois.name: Ubiquitous Chip
pois.description: Artistic brasserie dishes that display their provenance, served in a leafy space with fairy lights.

pois.name: Antonine Wall
pois.intro: The Antonine Wall was a turf fortification on stone foundations, built by the Romans across what is now the Central Belt of Scotland, between the Firth of Clyde and the Firth of Forth. Built some twenty years after Hadrian's Wall to the south, and intended to supersede it, while it was garrisoned it was the northernmost frontier barrier of the Roman Empire.

pois.name: Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum
pois.intro: Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum owned by Glasgow City Council is a major art gallery and museum in the Yorkhill area of Glasgow, Scotland, managed by Glasgow Museums. It is located in Kelvingrove Park in the West End of the city.

pois.name: Riverside Museum
pois.intro: The Riverside Museum is a museum in the Partick area of Glasgow, Scotland, housed in a building designed by Zaha Hadid Architects, with its River Clyde frontage at the new Pointhouse Quay. It forms part of the Glasgow Harbour regeneration project.

pois.name: Gallery of Modern Art
pois.intro: The Gallery of Modern Art is the main gallery of contemporary art in Glasgow, Scotland. GoMA offers a programme of temporary exhibitions and workshops.

pois.name: George Square
pois.intro: George Square is the principal civic square in the city of Glasgow, Scotland. It is one of six squares in the city centre, the others being Cathedral Square, St Andrew's Square, St Enoch Square, Royal Exchange Square, and Blythswood Square on Blythswood Hill.

pois.name: Glasgow Green
pois.intro: Glasgow Green is a park in the east end of Glasgow, Scotland, on the north bank of the River Clyde. Established in the 15th century, it is the oldest park in the city.

pois.name: The Burrell Collection
pois.intro: The Burrell Collection is a museum in Glasgow, Scotland, managed by Glasgow Museums. It houses the art collection of Sir William Burrell and Constance, Lady Burrell.

pois.name: Kelvingrove Park
pois.intro: Kelvingrove Park is a public park located on the River Kelvin in the West End of the city of Glasgow, Scotland, containing the Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum.

pois.name: Hunterian Museum
pois.intro: The Hunterian is a complex of museums located in and operated by the University of Glasgow in Glasgow, Scotland. It is the oldest museum in Scotland.

pois.name: Glasgow Science Centre
pois.intro: Glasgow Science Centre is a visitor attraction located in the Clyde Waterfront Regeneration area on the south bank of the River Clyde in Glasgow, Scotland. Queen Elizabeth II opened Glasgow Science Centre on 5 July 2001.

pois.name: Crookston Castle
pois.intro: Crookston Castle is a ruined medieval castle in the Pollok area of Glasgow, Scotland. It is located some five miles south-west of the city centre, on a hill overlooking the Levern Water, just before its confluence with the White Cart Water.

pois.name: Finnieston Crane
pois.intro: The Finnieston Crane or Stobcross Crane is a disused giant cantilever crane in the centre of Glasgow, Scotland. It is no longer operational, but is retained as a symbol of the city's engineering heritage.

pois.name: Mackintosh at the Willow
pois.intro: The Willow Tearooms are tearooms at 217 Sauchiehall Street, Glasgow, Scotland, designed by internationally renowned architect Charles Rennie Mackintosh, which opened for business in October 1903. They quickly gained enormous popularity, and are the most famous of the many Glasgow tearooms that opened in the late 19th and early 20th century.

pois.name: Cathkin Park
pois.intro: Cathkin Park is a municipal park in Glasgow, Scotland. The park is maintained by the city's parks department, and it is a public place where football is still played.

pois.name: Kelvinhall
pois.intro: Kelvinhall, known as Partick Cross until 1977, is an underground station on the Glasgow Subway, renamed after the nearby Kelvin Hall.

pois.name: Scotland Street School Museum
pois.intro: Scotland Street School Museum is a museum of school education in Glasgow, Scotland, in the district of Kingston. It is located in a former school designed by Charles Rennie Mackintosh between 1903 and 1906.

pois.name: The Lighthouse
pois.intro: The Lighthouse is the renamed, A-listed conversion of the former offices of the Glasgow Herald newspaper. Completed in 1895, it was designed by the architect Charles Rennie Mackintosh.

pois.name: Antonine Wall
pois.intro: The Antonine Wall was a turf fortification on stone foundations, built by the Romans across what is now the Central Belt of Scotland, between the Firth of Clyde and the Firth of Forth. Built some twenty years after Hadrian's Wall to the south, and intended to supersede it, while it was garrisoned it was the northernmost frontier barrier of the Roman Empire.

pois.name: People's Palace
pois.intro: The People's Palace and Winter Gardens in Glasgow, Scotland, is a museum and glasshouse situated in Glasgow Green, and was opened on 22 January 1898 by The 5th Earl of Rosebery.

pois.name: Provand's Lordship
pois.intro: Provand's Lordship is a medieval historic house museum in Glasgow, Scotland. It is in the Townhead area, at the top of Castle Street within sight of Glasgow Cathedral and next to the St Mungo Museum of Religious Life and Art.

pois.name: St Mungo Museum of Religious Life & Art
pois.wikipedia: en:St Mungo Museum of Religious Life and Art
pois.intro: The St Mungo Museum of Religious Life and Art is a museum of religion in Glasgow, Scotland. It is the only museum dedicated to religion and art in the British Isles.

pois.name: The Tenement House
pois.intro: The Tenement House is a historic house museum in Glasgow, owned and operated by the National Trust for Scotland. It is located at 145 Buccleuch Street, in the Garnethill area, near Charing Cross railway station and Cowcaddens subway station.

pois.name: Sharmanka Kinetic Theatre/Gallery
pois.description: A theatre of kinetic sculpture, where hundreds of carved figures and pieces of old scrap perform an incredible choreography to haunting music and synchronised light.
pois.intro: The Sharmanka Kinetic Gallery is a theatre of kinetic sculpture, in Glasgow, Scotland. The museum features mechanical figures which perform shows.

pois.name: Hunterian Art Gallery
pois.wikipedia: en:Hunterian Museum and Art Gallery#Hunterian Art Gallery

pois.name: Glenlee
pois.intro: Glenlee is a steel-hulled three-masted barque, built as a cargo ship at Port Glasgow under that name in 1896 for Glasgow owners. With later owners she was named Islamount and Clarastella.

pois.name: Chaophraya
pois.intro: Unter der Adresse 4 Nelson Mandela Place in der schottischen Stadt Glasgow befindet sich ein Geschäftsgebäude. 1970 wurde das Bauwerk als Einzeldenkmal in die schottischen Denkmallisten zunächst in der Kategorie B aufgenommen.

pois.name: The Hidden Lane Tearoom
pois.description: Vintage tearoom serving afternoon tea, sandwiches, soups, a selection of home-made cakes and over 30 loose-leaf teas and freshly ground coffee.

pois.name: Massawa
pois.description: Vibrant flavours and warm hospitality of Eritrean and Ethiopian cuisine.

pois.name: Punjabi Rasoi
pois.description: Indian takeaway from the owners of the Little Curry House on Byres Road.

pois.name: Brewhaus
pois.intro: Crosslands was a public house in the Maryhill area of Glasgow, Scotland, that featured in the 1996 film Trainspotting. It is now known as BrewHaus.

pois.name: Naked Soup
pois.description: Cafe serving freshly made sandwiches, soups, and all-day breakfasts.

pois.name: Category Is Books
pois.intro: Category Is Books is an independent bookshop in Glasgow, Scotland. It is one of only two LGBT+ bookshop in Scotland and one of only eight in the United Kingdom.

pois.name: Voltaire and Rousseau
pois.description: Established secondhand store selling academic books, fiction, literary criticism and rare editions.

pois.name: Roots, Fruits & Flowers: Fruit & Veg Merchant
pois.description: Fruit and vegetable merchant stocked daily from local markets with seasonal produce.

pois.name: Mellis
pois.description: Cheesemonger selling a range of fine farmhouse and artisan cheeses.

pois.name: 'In Bloom' by Grisel Illustrations
pois.description: ''IN BLOOM' by Grisel illustrations is an open illustration studio, retail shop and art gallery. Grisel exhibits her work at the same time that you can see how she works. Art prints, framed or unframed artwork, home decor such as mugs, tote bags, clothing

pois.name: Achilles Heel
pois.description: Dedicated running store selling road and track shoes, athletes' clothing, equipment and accessories.

pois.name: Bird & Blend Tea Co. Glasgow Shop
pois.description: Tea shop with a great selection of different teas.

pois.name: Opal Moon
pois.description: Incense, oils, jewellery, crystals, gemstones, cards, books, and all other types of spiritual and New Age gifts and supplies.

pois.name: Queen's Park
pois.intro: Queen's Park is a park situated on the south side of the city of Glasgow, Scotland, between Strathbungo, Shawlands, Battlefield, Mount Florida, and Crosshill.

pois.name: Blythswood Square Gardens
pois.intro: Blythswood Square is the Georgian square on Blythswood Hill in the heart of the City of Glasgow, Scotland. The square is part of the 'Magnificent New Town of Blythswood' built in the 1800s on the rising empty ground west of a very new Buchanan Street.

pois.name: Bellahouston Park
pois.intro: Bellahouston Park is a public park in the Bellahouston district on the South Side of Glasgow, Scotland, between the areas of Craigton, Dumbreck, Ibrox and Mosspark covering an area of 71 hectares. The main part of Bellahouston Park was acquired by Glasgow Corporation in 1895 for the sum of £50,000, and opened to the public in 1896.

pois.name: Pollok Country Park
pois.intro: Pollok Country Park is a 146-hectare country park located between Shawlands, Crossmyloof, and Pollok in Glasgow, Scotland. In 2007, Pollok Country Park was named Britain's Best Park, and in 2008 it was named the Best Park in Europe, beating competition from parks in Italy, France, Germany, Poland and Sweden.

pois.name: Dawsholm Park Local Nature Reserve
pois.intro: Dawsholm Park is a public park in Glasgow, Scotland, adjoining the Kelvindale, Maryhill and Temple areas of the city, and southern parts of the town of Bearsden. It is situated on the River Kelvin, north of the River Clyde.

pois.name: Ruchill Park
pois.intro: Ruchill Park is a public park in Ruchill, Glasgow, Scotland, approximately 2 miles north-west of the city centre. It is adjacent to the former location of Ruchill Hospital on Bilsland Drive.

pois.name: Possil Marsh Nature Reserve
pois.intro: Possil Marsh is a nature reserve and Site of Special Scientific Interest, of both flora and fauna, within the city of Glasgow, Scotland. The reserve was once part of an extensive system of lochs and marshes which extended throughout much of lowland West Central Scotland.

pois.name: Elizabeth Street Park
pois.description: landscaped area with seats and dog park

pois.name: Princes Square
pois.intro: Princes Square is a shopping centre on Buchanan Street in central Glasgow, Scotland. It was first designed and built in the 1840s by John Baird and other architects.

pois.name: Royal Exchange Square
pois.intro: The Royal Exchange Square is a public square in Glasgow, Scotland. The square lies between Buchanan Street and Queen Street, opening out Queen Street and Ingram Street to the south of George Square.

pois.name: Play It Again Records
pois.openingHours: Most days after 15:00 or 16:00, depends on when the owner comes by

pois.name: St Andrew's Square
pois.intro: St Andrew's Square is a public square in the city of Glasgow, Scotland and lies to the south east corner of Glasgow Cross, close to Glasgow Green. The square is noted for its immense 18th-century classical church, St Andrew's in the Square, from which the square takes its name.

pois.name: Haggs Castle
pois.intro: Haggs Castle is a 16th-century tower house, located in the neighbourhood of Pollokshields, in Glasgow, Scotland. The richly decorated building was restored in the 19th century, and today is once more occupied as a residence.

terminalResolution.notes: Ships dock at Greenock Ocean Terminal, about 32 km from Glasgow. Kept as a gateway port, renamed Glasgow (Greenock). It shares its terminal with the Greenock entry. Moved the Greenock Ocean Terminal pin about 900 m onto the terminal building (two Google Maps listings agree).
